The students in the middle desks have a lower level of listening comprehension and a reduced vision of the board, while the stud ents at the back have the least understanding of the words and the poorest vision of the board. In this scenario, the students essentially serve as nominal entities with no grasp of the subject matter, akin to test masses in gravity. xxi)By analogy, the region around a body within which its gravitational pull is perceptible is the gravitational field. The gravitational field intensity (or strength), E, of a body at a point inside the field is the force experienced by a unit test mass placed at that point. Consequently, the unit test mass does not alter the field configuration of the body. Q: 1. What is the difference between gravitational force and gravitational field strength?

Ans: Gravitational field strength is the force experienced by a unit mass at that point of interest. Gravitational force is the amount of force acting on a body. It is the product of field strength times the mass under consideration. Gravitational pull is just a more colloquial name for gravitational force.

Q 2. Why is gravitational field strength different? The more the mass of an object, the greater the gravitational field it has. The Earth hence has a greater gravitational field than the Moon. The Moon is attracted to the Earth because it is within the Earth's gravitational field.
